sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][D153][F6][D192][F7][D232].
The FY2022 jump came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
Revenue then declined three straight years, by 16.5%, 1.8% and 4.6%, to $184 billion in FY2025 [F8][D274][F9][D316][F10][D358].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth as it fell 5.3% [D402][D404][D403].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and +1.5pp of growth on a 16.5% increase [D418][D420][D419].
The FY2025 revenue decline came mainly from lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes [P17].
Operating costs grew 1.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 3.4% [D379][D373].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% against a 30.5% net income decline as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D361][D359][D374].
Net margin of 6.7% in FY2025 sat below the 7.9% window median and far below the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Net margin fell 2.5pp in FY2025, with cost of revenue at 57.2% of revenue against 58.8% in FY2024 [D369][D338][D296].
Higher upstream depreciation, lower realizations and higher operating costs drove the earnings decline [P9].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% in FY2025 from 35.5% in FY2024 [D345][D303].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income in FY2025, above the 1.97x window median [F60][D346][D644].
Higher cash distributions from TCO and legacy Hess assets more than offset lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow of $16.6 billion was an 8.8% margin, below the 8.9% window median [F80][D343][D616].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F70][D342][D348].
Cash and investments were $7.3 billion at FY2025, down 11.8% [D349][D375].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so total debt and net cash are omitted for later years [X193].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D353][D354].
Return on average equity of 7.3% ranked in the 17th percentile of six energy peers against a 14.9% median [D357][D641][D642].
Revenue declined in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, from $197 billion to $184 billion [R1][F8][F10].
Three years of falling revenue leave the top line dependent on commodity prices rather than volume growth [R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 149.7% in FY2025 [R4][D270][D312][D354].
Payouts above free cash flow draw on the balance sheet and limit the cushion if prices stay weak [R4].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for FY2018 through FY2025, for example FY2025 at $184 billion against $189 billion as first reported [R3][F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix recast and first-reported years are not like-for-like [R3].
If FY2026 revenue falls below the FY2025 level of $184 billion, the three-year decline continues; it will appear in the FY2026 10-K [F10].
If buybacks and dividends stay above 100% of free cash flow, against 149.7% in FY2025, the payout remains uncovered [D354].
If net margin falls below the 7.9% window median, the FY2025 level of 6.7% would mark a further step down [F30][D613].
